research_question: Does Mendes / Djedet / Tell el-Rub'a contain an object, container, burial assemblage, or museum-provenanced fragment that bridges the Mendesian Osiris-phallus relic tradition to a physical candidate class?
method_rule: Independent convergence raises search priority but is not proof. Search only catalogs, excavation archives, museum records, publications, conservation reports and non-destructive imaging; no illicit excavation or removal.
why_mendes: Mendes is the cult center of Banebdjedet and a major Mendesian religious node.
Prior source work in this project places the Mendesian relic tradition in the phallus/spine branch of Osirian religious geography.
Museum collections preserve identifiable Mendes excavation assemblages that can be provenance-rewound object by object.

first_pass_findings.finding: The Met records a 1902 Mendes burial of priest Nesbanebdjedet. One chamber was nearly empty except for fragments of gold leaf; another context contained more than 360 shabtis, fragments, several amulets, and a mummy decorated with gold-leaf trappings, with Cairo CG 53465-53469 cited for the mummy equipment.
first_pass_findings.search_consequence: Audit the complete 1902 assemblage, especially amulets, gold-leaf fragments, mummy trappings, unillustrated fragments, object cards, and Cairo CG 53465-53469. Do not infer relic identity from gold alone.

first_pass_findings.finding: The British Museum place index for Tell el-Ruba / Mendes currently links 15 collection objects, including figures and multiple shabtis with Mendes/Tell el-Ruba findspot associations.
first_pass_findings.search_consequence: Enumerate all 15 records and inspect provenance wording, conservation history, materials, unexplained attachments, cavities, fragments, and associated excavation references.

first_pass_findings.finding: The Met notes that the Nesbanebdjedet shabtis and related burial material became dispersed across Egypt, museums, and private collections.
first_pass_findings.search_consequence: Treat the assemblage as a distributed provenance graph rather than one museum collection; reconstruct sister objects by inscription, dimensions, excavation year and priest name.

next_queries: Cairo CG 53465-53469 complete catalog entries, drawings, photographs and conservation history
1902 Aly Habib / Egyptian Antiquities Service Mendes excavation report and object lists
all amulets associated with Nesbanebdjedet burial
all gold-leaf fragments or trappings from the nearly empty chamber and mummy
British Museum Tell el-Ruba 15-object complete audit
Mendes / Banebdjedet objects with X-ray, CT, radiography or conservation imaging
objects from Mendes catalogued as fragment, unidentified, fitting, insert, plaque, amulet, pendant, vessel or reliquary

upgrade_to_bridge_candidate_if: independent Osirian or Banebdjedet ritual association
or sealed/internal structure supported by imaging or conservation records

claim_ceiling: This pass prioritizes Mendes for documentary and museum research. It does not establish the existence, survival, location, or divine identity of a physical Osiris phallus relic.
